LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Denver Broncos play host to the Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos are coming off their third win in the last four games, though it required a late, game-winning drive against the decrepit division rival Los Angeles Chargers . The return of Sean Payton as play-caller didn't exactly result in an explosive or efficient offense, but the Broncos did just enough to hold off L.A. and climb back over .500. The Seahawks, meanwhile, dropped to 3-2 after falling to their own division rivals in the San Francisco 49ers . The Niners moved the ball quite well against the vaunted Seattle defense, and turnovers in their own territory haunted the Seahawks and ultimately cost them the game. Will the Seahawks bounce back, or will the Broncos capture their second consecutive victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Broncos vs. Seahawks live Date: Thursday, Oct. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Empower Field at Mile High (Denver) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Seahawks have the ball Let's start here: the Seahawks cannot run the ball at all. They couldn't run the ball when rookie running back Jadarian Price was healthy earlier in the season, and they haven't been able to run the ball since he's been out. The trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has combined for just 447 yards on 127 carries -- an average of just 3.5 per tote. The Seahawks do not get much push up front, as their backs average a mere 0.69 yards before contact per carry, a figure that ranks fourth-worst in the NFL , according to Tru Media. Their 2.83 yards after contact per carry is more respectable, ranking 14th league-wide. The Broncos will have to be careful there. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league so far (0.59), but the most rushing yards after contact (3.92), thanks to a sky-high avoided tackle rate by enemy backs (30.1%). Much of that production came from Kenneth Walker III in the season opener, but even in Weeks 2 through 5, the Broncos rank in the bottom third of the league in both yards after contact per attempt and broken tackle rate. Wilson is likely to be the primary runner once again while Price and Zach Charbonnet remain sidelined. The Broncos will have to get him on the ground on the first try, limiting the yards he can gain after contact, because the Seahawks just don't create much for him in the first place. He scarcely gets more than is blocked without breaking through tackles. In the passing game, Sam Darnold has struggled to replicate last year's results -- especially over the last two weeks. In games against the Chargers and 49ers, Darnold went just 31-of-51 for 363 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. After leading the league in turnovers last season, Darnold has already been picked off five times in his three full appearances this season, while his yards per attempt average is down from 8.5 to just 7.7. His completion rate is down over 3 percentage points as well. Denver's pass defense has been largely good so far this year, with the Broncos ranking fifth in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media. The Broncos just held the Chargers to 82 net passing yards last week, which plays a huge role in that figure, but they've also allowed only one team ( Rams ) to top 218 net passing yards in any game so far. (The Chiefs didn't have to throw the ball very much in Week 1, though, because they did whatever they wanted on the ground.) The Broncos won't have Patrick Surtain II or Talanoa Hufanga here, and Riley Moss is listed as questionable -- all of which is a significant issue when you're going up against Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL in both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine figure to see increased roles due to the cornerback injuries, while Devon Key will play more in the wake of Hufanga's absence. They'll all have their work cut out for them against JSN. The Seahawks really don't throw the ball to anyone else all that often. When the Broncos have the ball Denver might have gotten a win last week, but Sean Payton's return as play-caller didn't have much to do with it. The Broncos entered the game against the Chargers averaging a miserable 4.9 yards per play, then averaged a mere 3.9 per play in the win over Los Angeles. Bo Nix totaled just 123 yards on his 27 pass attempts, J.K. Dobbins ran for only 68 yards on his 18 carries, Jaylen Waddle caught just two of five balls thrown his way for just 19 yards ... nothing went well offensively. And nothing has gone right pretty much all year, with the exception of the second halves of the Broncos' wins over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3. Two good halves in five weeks isn't much to write home about, even if those halves helped the Broncos steal a pair of wins and arrive at 3-2. Nix is essentially refusing to push the ball down the field so far this season. His average air yards per attempt in each of his first two years of his career was 7.3, according to Tru Media, but that figure has dropped all the way to 5.2 this year. He threw deep on 13.1% of his passes as a rookie and 11.8% of them last year, but he's done so on only 7.4% of his attempts this season. Nix also isn't running anymore. He scrambled 27.3% of the time when pressured during his rookie season and 16.1% of the time last season. That number is all the way down to 5.6% so far this year, meaning he's scrambled only four times in five games. All of this, combined with his insistence on checking down repeatedly, has made the pass offense feel neutered to date. Meanwhile, the Broncos also can't run the ball. Dobbins looks like he's running with a piano on his back, slogging his way to 3.6 yards per carry. RJ Harvey barely gets opportunities, but he hasn't done any better at only 3.7 yards per carry. Harvey is at least productive in the short passing game, but the Broncos de-emphasized that last week under Payton in favor of more Dobbins runs that went nowhere. The Seahawks have largely been their usual selves defensively through the first five weeks of the season. They've arrived at their two losses largely by virtue of their offense repeatedly turning the ball over against the Commanders (three times) and 49ers (four, including a fumble that resulted in a touchdown). Seattle has held opponents to the fewest passing yards in the league and the fewest net yards per attempt, and it has limited running games to the eighth-fewest yards per attempt as well. It's hard to see the Broncos snapping out of their funk against this unit. Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have let the Broncos come away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Surtain here, which is obviously a problem against JSN. away.headline: Rams' mounting injuries could strip playoff stakes from Seahawks games

away.blurb: McVay also confirmed that starting defensive tackles Poona Ford and Kobie Turner will miss extended time , and that newly signed kicker Blake Grupe suffered a torn ACL in that game and will miss the rest of the season. It doesn’t end there — McVay also mentioned that defensive end Myles Garrett will not return to practice this week, and cornerback Trent McDuffie is “progressing but uncertain” for Week 7. After being eliminated from the playoffs by the eventual NFC champion in back-to-back seasons, the Rams went all-in on contending in 2026. They gave up a haul, including their 2027 first-round draft pick, to acquire reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year Garrett from the Cleveland Browns . They traded their 2026 first-round pick to the Kansas City Chiefs for McDuffie to round out their defense. Without either of them available, they’ve sunk to the bottom of the division and are currently just 2-4. While the Seahawks’ worries are warranted — they’re disappointed in a 3-3 start and look as beatable as they did at any point last year — they just need to look at the Rams to remind themselves: It could always be worse. They have all their draft picks and expect to return reinforcements to their running back room in the coming weeks in the form of Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price. The NFL scheduled these two teams in Weeks 16 and 18, expecting those games to be as anticipated as any this season. At this point, though, one or both teams could be out of the playoff race entirely. While the Seattle Seahawks have faced their fair share of trials and tribulations thus far in 2026, even they can’t hold a candle to the injury problem plaguing their NFC West rival Los Angeles Rams . On Monday afternoon, Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters that star wide receiver Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6 and will miss 6-10 weeks. It'll be at least two weeks until Jadarian Price is eligible to return from injured reserve, while Zach Charbonnet has a chance to play against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7. Mike Macdonald revealed a little bit of a timeline as far as Price's return during his Friday morning show with Brock and Salk on Seattle Sports 710 . "He's doing great," Macdonald said. "We should be looking at a sooner rather than later return after this [Kansas City Chiefs] game." Price has been out since the start of Week 4 with a chest injury, which he aggravated in practice after getting the initial injury in Week 2 against the Arizona Cardinals. The rookie out of Notre Dame has had a couple of costly fumbles , but since George Holani and Emanuel Wilson have also since lost a combined three fumbles, he's hardly the only culprit. Price has offered some explosiveness in the run game in a limited sample size, and his speed is what the main running back room lacks. Mookie Alexander Sat, October 17, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Mike Macdonald had no update on Charbonnet's progress (or, maybe, no update he was willing to share), but it's worth noting that Charbonnet must be activated this upcoming week or else he reverts to injured reserve for the rest of the season. Seattle opened his 21-day practice window on Oct. 1, prior to the Week 4 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Once that window expires, the Seahawks either have to place him on the 53-man roster or end his season. The latter is obviously not happening unless there's some unbelievably worrying setback, so we're left to turn our attention to Price. In an ideal world, Charbonnet is back in Week 7 and Price is back in Week 8, at which point the running back room should be a lot stronger.

home.headline: Report suggests Broncos QB Bo Nix is worried about injuring his ankle again
home.blurb: “I don’t understand why we can’t really push the ball vertically right now," Nix said. "Defenses are just sitting back there hanging out. We’re just going to keep running the football. Hopefully you have to find ways to get more out of it.” Six games into the 2026 NFL season, Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix ranks 32nd in the NFL with an average of 5.6 yards per passing attempt. Nix's struggles and inability (or unwillingness) to throw the ball downfield have been well-documented this season, and the QB was asked about it following the team's 17-14 win over the Seattle Seahawks last Thursday. Some fans and pundits have speculated that Nix's struggles are related to the ankle injury Nix suffered during the NFL playoffs last season. Not so much the physical fallout , but Nix's ability to get over the injury mentally. When asked if Nix is struggling to mentally move past his injury during his Monday conference call, Broncos coach Sean Payton essentially sidestepped the question, saying the QB has done a good job overcoming adversity in his career. "All the other things relative to the mental toughness, the mental fortitude — this is a tough league," Payton said . "We hit every aspect, and I think that’s one of the things that attracted us to Bo in the beginning is we had seen his ability to climb through adversity. It’s not just Bo that feels that. Right now, offensively, I feel that, our players feel that and we’ll improve.” Publicly, Payton didn't suggest Nix is struggling to get over his injury mentally. Meanwhile, somebody (presumably within the organization) has leaked to James Palmer of NFL on Prime Video that the club believes Nix is playing "a bit gun shy." "[T]here is a difference with Nix in 2026, where Nix is focused on not losing the game more than winning the game," Palmer tweeted on Monday . "Don't turn the ball over. Don't be the reason why we lose the game. That's kind of manifested in his mind to the point that the conservative approach has become an issue on the field." Palmer's lengthy tweet also included this: Nix is healthy, and the ankle is fine . But returning from an injury is also not cut and dry and takes time. The Broncos want Nix to run it more and they're seeing a player that is a bit gun shy right now. If you look at the runs that Denver has dialed up, a lot of them he's looking for the sidelines and he's looking for a way to get down as soon as possible. He's not looking for the extra yards or the needed yards in key situations. It's been frustrating. Palmer later suggested that Nix is "seeing ghosts at times," and the team is "obviously concerned with the funk he's currently stuck in." And this is perhaps the most notable part of the report : "They'd love to see him take a couple of big hits and realize he's not going to get hurt, the ankle is good, remember you're a tough football player." home.headline: Rams hosting two ex-Broncos kickers after Blake Grupe injury
home.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
home.blurb: After Harrison Mevis missed a field goal attempt and had another kick blocked last week, the Rams cut Mevis and replaced him with Blake Grupe. In his first game with L.A., Grupe tore his ACL on Sunday, ruling him out for the rest of the season. Punter Ethan Evans took over kicking duties after Grupe went down on Sunday. The Los Angeles Rams have quite the dilemma at kicker. The Rams are now scrambling to find a new kicker ahead of their game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Oct. 25. L.A. will bring in two veteran kickers on Tuesday, both of whom spent time with the Denver Broncos . The Rams are set to host Brandon McManus and Matt Prater for workouts, according to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo . Prater played in Denver from 2007-2014, setting a then-NFL record with a 64-yard field goal in 2013. Prater was replaced by McManus midway through the 2014 campaign. McManus went on to spend nine years with the Broncos , helping the team win Super Bowl 50 following the 2015 season. Prater is now 42 and McManus is 35. We'll see if either kicker ends up signing with L.A. this week. Social : Follow Broncos Wire on Facebook and Twitter/X ! The Jags are playing their second consecutive international games, both taking place in London. They defeated the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last week. The last-second win put them at 4-1 on the season, tied for the second-best record in the AFC. The Texans come in with a bit different standing, sitting at 1-4, though, like the Jags, they are also coming off a win. Houston got their first win against the Tennessee Titans , who now sit at 0-5. Texans vs. Jaguars need to know Jaguars London history: The Jags are pretty much London's home team, playing there at least once a year since 2013, with the exception of 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic, with an 8-7 record across the pond. Their first-ever game in England was in 2013, a loss to the 49ers at Wembley Stadium. Their first international win was their third of the kind, a 2015 game against the Bills . And of course, their most recent win came in Week 5 against the Eagles. Marvin Harrison Jr. : The biggest news out of Houston is the addition of former No. 4 overall pick Marvin Harrison Jr. joining the team. Harrison's time with the Arizona Cardinals didn't work out as expected, but he and the Texans are hoping a fresh start will be reflected in his stat line. What should help the WR make a quick adjustment to his new team is the reunion with quarterback C.J. Stroud , who he had great success with at Ohio State. Harrison will be one to watch this week as the Texans offense has the tall task of keeping up with a solid Jaguars offense. Stroud has played well despite their record, so adding Harrison could be huge for the Texans' offense. Jaguars o-line vs. Texans defense: The Jags will be without left tackle Anton Harrison , who needs surgery. The offensive line will be going up against defensive end Will Anderson Jr. , who has 27 total tackles, 7.5 sacks, a league high, and one forced fumble and recovery this season. The Jags need to protect Trevor Lawrence, especially so he can continue to improve in his game-time decisions. The Jags are now 4-1 in the 2026 season and are 8-7 all-time in their games in London. That puts them in a great spot to win the AFC South this season, as they have a two-game lead over the Indianapolis Colts and a three-game lead over Houston, which picked up its first win of the season in Week 5. The Texans started the year 0-4 against a tough schedule, but they blew out the Tennessee Titans last Sunday – a potential sign of good things to come. C.J. Stroud and company also have a new weapon, as former top-five pick Marvin Harrison Jr. was traded from the Arizona Cardinals to Houston following Sunday's win. The Texans' defense is going to have to be better in the 2026 season if they're going to make the playoffs, and Houston was the No. 1 defense in EPA per play in 2025. It simply hasn't found that level in the 2026 campaign, and things won't be easy against a Jacksonville offense that is currently sixth in the NFL in EPA/Play. Trevor Lawrence has put himself in the MVP conversation this season, sitting fourth in the odds heading into this matchup. There's nothing better than a standalone game to open our Sunday, and this AFC South battle has major playoff implications, especially if Houston is able to pull off the upset. Oddsmakers have the Jags favored by three points in London, where they have played more games than any other franchise, going 8-7 across 15 matchups. All week long, the SI Betting team has been making game picks, player props, and a few anytime touchdown scorer selections to help bettors get the most out of this London matchup. The NFL has been loaded with international games this season, and they've had some wild results. Should we expect more of the same in Week 6? The Texans got off to a terrible start to the season, while the Jaguars got off to a red-hot start, but don't be surprised if things begin to trend in opposite directions starting this weekend. The Jaguars rank 10th in offensive luck and second in defensive luck according to RBSDM.com, while the Texans rank outside the top 10 in that metric on both sides of the ball. Defensively, the Texans outrank the Jaguars in success rate, but Jacksonville comes out on top when it comes to opponent EPA. That tells us that the Jaguars haven't been as good on a down-to-down basis, but they've allowed fewer explosive plays. I trust success rate a lot more when it comes to consistent, long-term results, so I'm giving a nod to Houston in that area. It can't be overstated how different the Texans' offense is with Nico Collins healthy. They scored 31, 30, and 26 points in the three games he played in, but six and 17 points in their two games without him. I expect the Texans to move the ball through the air in Week 6, and Collins has been a major threat to score, finding the end zone 21 times over the last three completed seasons. He’s worth a shot at +165 for a Houston offense that is down several playmakers due to injury. Jaguars star receiver Parker Washington has found the end zone in three of his five games this season, hitting paydirt four times in total. The clear No. 1 option in this Jacksonville offense, Washington has played 77.5 percent of the Jags’ offensive snaps, catching 22 of his 35 targets for 352 yards. Parker Washington Anytime TD (+180) Jaguars star receiver Parker Washington has found the end zone in three of his five games this season, hitting paydirt four times in total. The clear No. 1 option in this Jacksonville offense, Washington has played 77.5 percent of the Jags’ offensive snaps, catching 22 of his 35 targets for 352 yards. Not only that, but Washington has made some ridiculous grabs – including his touchdown in Week 5 – to bail out Trevor Lawrence. Jacksonville’s passing offense hits a ton of big plays and ranks No. 3 in the NFL in EPA/Pass. I love this price for Washington (nearly 2/1) since no other Jags receiver has been a consistent threat to lead the team in targets. Nico Collins Anytime TD (+165) Texans No. 1 receiver Nico Collins has found the end zone in two of his three appearances this season, catching three scores overall. He’s been targeted 25 times by C.J. Stroud, reeling in 19 of those for 249 yards. I actually like this matchup for Collins, even though the Jags have allowed just four passing touchdowns in 2026. Jacksonville has also given up the third-most passing yards in the NFL and ranks outside the top-20 in the league in yards per play allowed. I expect the Texans to move the ball through the air in Week 6, and Collins has been a major threat to score, finding the end zone 21 times over the last three completed seasons. away.headline: Chicago Bears DE Montez Sweat suspended for violating NFL performance-enhancing substances policy
away.blurb: Updated on: October 13, 2026 / 3:19 PM CDT / CBS Chicago Chicago Bears defensive end Montez Sweat is suspended for the team's next two games without pay for violating the NFL's performance-enhancing substances policy, the NFL said Tuesday. The NFL did not specify further details about what Sweat is accused of doing or what kind of drugs he is accused of taking. This means Sweat will not play with the Bears when they take on the Atlanta Falcons this coming Sunday, nor when they take on the New England Patriots on Thursday of next week. He will be eligible for reinstatement on Friday, Oct. 23, after the Bears-Patriots game. In the next game after that, the Bears take on the Seattle Seahawks. The Bears acquired the rusher Sweat from the Washington Commanders in the fall of 2023.

away.headline: Chicago Bears reunite with defensive back ahead of Week 7 game vs. Patriots
away.blurb: The Bears are also dealing with an injury in their cornerbacks room with Tyrique Stevenson, who is battling a hip issue . Stevenson was able to practice on a limited basis throughout last week and had a questionable tag but was ultimately inactive for Sunday's game. Given the fact that Stevenson practiced on a limited basis last week tells us he has a decent chance to return in Week 7, but playing on a short week might complicate things. We'll know more about Stevenson's status on Monday and over the next few days, when the Bears put out their injury reports. Even when he returns, Stevenson isn't going to have much of a role. Gordon's return puts him back in the slot, and that moves Malik Muhammad to the boundary opposite Jaylon Johnson. The Bears Aren't Afforded the Luxury of Slow-Playing Kyler Gordon's Return The Chicago Bears are making an addition to their practice squad ahead of the Week 7 game against the New England Patriots on Thursday night. The Bears announced on Monday that they have signed defensive back KC Eziomume to the practice squad. Eziomume was with the Bears during the offseason before he came down with an injury that led to him being waived with an injury designation on Aug. 8. Eziomume was one of the Bears' initial 2026 undrafted free-agent signings. He played his final season of college ball at Tulane and tallied one pass break-up in seven contests. Prior to his stint at Tulane, the 6-foot-1, 198-pound defensive back appeared in four games with Alabama A&M, totaling five tackles. If Eziomume is able to get into a game for the Bears, he will be making his NFL debut. He did not play a snap during the preseason, as his injury occurred before Week 1. An addition amid recent moves, injury Eziomume will be taking the practice squad spot of cornerback Nick McCloud, who was promoted to the active roster over the weekend on the same day veteran safety Xavier Woods was waived. It was surprising to see the Bears cut Woods loose. After all, he had started in two games this season and was playing a key role with the Bears dealing with injuries in the secondary. Woods was waived on the same day slot cornerback Kyler Gordon was activated off the physically unable to perform list. The Bears are still going to need some snaps from Muhammad in the slot until Gordon is fully ramped up, something defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said could take more time . home.blurb: The Bears conducted their final practice of the week, which included final game designations for Sunday. Quarterback Caleb Williams practiced in full for a third straight day, an indication that he's poised to return to the lineup in Week 6. But Williams, who's missed the last three games, is questionable. There are some last step hurdles for him to clear, but all indications are he will be under center vs. the Falcons. Elsewhere, cornerback Kyler Gordon was also a full participant in practice all week, and he's questionable for Sunday's game as he looks to return from the PUP list. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. Ravens QB Lamar Jackson has a realistic chance to return for Sunday’s game at Cleveland, per league source. pic.twitter.com/O82hES7z4t After the Ravens opened as 3.5-point favorites against the Browns on Sunday night, that line has moved to 4.5 and now all the way to 5.5 following Adam Schefter's report. DraftKings Sportsbook has the Ravens as 5.5-point favorites, a full one-point change from where the spread was on Tuesday morning . Still, Jackson didn't practice on Wednesday, which makes his status for Sunday a little murky. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that the two-time league MVP is "day-to-day." Minter said that Lamar Jackson remains “day to day” and when he’s ready, he’ll be out at practice. While it would have been a positive sign for the Ravens for Jackson to practice on Wednesday, he still has time to log a session on Thursday or Friday before the team's matchup against Cleveland. Sports Illustrated spoke to multiple oddsmakers about Jackosn's status and how it could impact this game. "Looking at this line, we are expecting Lamar to play," Christian Cipollini, Senior Trading Manager at BetMGM , told Sports Illustrated . "It will drop to under three if Lamar ends up being out. No change for Baltimore, Snoop (Tyler Huntley) is a capable backup who has similar strengths to Lamar. They do not need to change their offense when Lamar is out which is very helpful." On Wednesday, Fanatics Sportsbook explained to Sports Illustrated that they actually dropped their line from 5.5 to Ravens -5 after Jackson missed practice. “We're sitting at five on our site,” Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated. “As it currently stands as of this moment, and as Lamar's status becomes murkier, that will likely go further towards the Browns.” The market seems to be putting a lot of stock into Schefter's report, but that could change quickly if the star quarterback logs another DNP on Thursday. The Baltimore Ravens are no strangers to playing without their star quarterback, and that helps to explain why they're 3-point favorites on Sunday despite backup Tyler Huntley starting. My Ravens vs. Browns predictions back Baltimore to grind out a win while leaning on Derrick Henry, who can exploit a vulnerable Cleveland run defense. Here are my NFL picks ahead of this Sunday, Oct. 18, clash, with kickoff set for 1 p.m. ET today. Ravens vs Browns prediction today: Ravens -3.5 The Baltimore Ravens are chasing their fourth straight win over the Cleveland Browns , and Lamar Jackson's absence isn't deterring me from fading a Cleveland team that crashed back to earth last weekend. Even with Todd Monken's knowledge of his former team, I'll lay the points - playable anywhere from -3 to -4. Tyler Huntley , one of the NFL's better backup QBs, led Baltimore to an overtime win in Week 5, and he's now 3-0 as a starter since last season. But this pick is more about what Derrick Henry can do against a Browns defense that's allowing 117.4 rushing yards per game and could be without Carson Schwesinger and Mason Graham (both questionable). On the other side of the ball, look for the visitors to be opportunistic against Deshaun Watson , who was sacked eight times in Week 5 and may have to do more in the passing game given the hosts' backfield injuries. The Ravens are 4-2 ATS in their past six road games , and two of the last three meetings between these teams have been emphatic Baltimore blowouts. TOP PICK Ravens vs Browns player prop: Derrick Henry Over 88.5 rushing yards The Ravens have handed Henry a heavy workload once again this season - he leads the league with 113 carries while averaging 95.2 YPG on the ground, and yet there's room for more with Jackson sidelined. This AFC North duel is a favorable matchup for King Henry, too, with the Browns giving up 134 rushing yards last weekend in New York and dealing with injuries across the defensive line . I don't see that banged-up unit being a match for Baltimore's powerhouse RB, who sits third in the NFL in yards after contact (262). Henry has gone past this O/U number in eight of his last 10 outings , and a run-heavy script should produce 20+ carries. Ravens vs Browns combo The Ravens have scored 24+ points in each of their wins this year , and this line feels too low despite Jackson being sidelined. The Over is 7-3 in Baltimore's last 10 games, and it's been a winning ticket in the past five meetings between these teams . With Cleveland sweating on the health of key defensive playmakers, Huntley can deliver a similar stat line to his SNF effort against the Falcons (201 passing yards, two TD passes, no turnovers), while the Browns' offense is boosted by KC Concepcion clearing the concussion protocol. When Baltimore isn't riding Henry and the ground game, look for Mark Andrews to be a key checkdown option for Huntley. Andrews has 22 catches through five contests, and he's finished with 6+ targets in four of those outings . Ravens moneyline Mark Andrews Over 3.5 receptions Ravens vs Browns touchdown scorer: Harold Fannin Jr. The Browns feel likelier to have success through the air than on the ground on Sunday, and Harold Fannin Jr. stands out as an anytime TD pick after grabbing three scores already this year . Baltimore has given up three touchdowns to tight ends in the opening five weeks , and snap count shouldn't be an issue for Fannin Jr. after logging a 93% mark last weekend against the Jets. away.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
away.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. away.headline: Thursday injury report for the Browns Week 6 against the Ravens
away.blurb: After an overwhelming 11 players sat out on Wednesday, several key starters on the offensive line, defensive interior, and skill positions returned to the field in a limited or full capacity. Thursday provided major relief for the depth chart as four players upgraded from Wednesday’s DNP list to limited status. They join wide receivers Denzel Boston, Tylan Wallace, and KC Concepcion (concussion protocol), along with safety Grant Delpit, who all remained limited. Starting center Elgton Jenkins upgraded from limited on Wednesday to a full participant on Thursday, clearing any minor knee concern ahead of Sunday. Quarterback Dillon Gabriel maintained his full participation status as he continues to build momentum. Here is Thursday's full injury report breakdown as we progress through Week 6. away.headline: Ravens Final Week 6 Injury Report: Four Players Ruled Out
away.blurb: Ravens Final Week 6 Injury Report: Four Players Ruled Out - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Hurts reportedly out for season Ravens Final Week 6 Injury Report: Four Players Ruled Out While it had been established that the Ravens would likely be without quarterback Lamar Jackson for another game, he has officially been ruled out, along with three others. Center Cam Jurgens also remains out as he works his way back from concussion protocol. The Ravens traded for the former Philadelphia Eagles center before Week 5, but he was in the protocol when the trade took place. With Jurgens out, this means rookie guard Vega Ioane will step in as the center yet again. Additionally, guard Andrew Vorhees is questionable with a foot injury, and he may need more time to heal as well. Emery Jones Jr. may get the start on Sunday, especially so as not to lead to a further injury for Vorhees. The issue is that Jones is also questionable, pointing to what could be an issue if both are not able to play. Finally, defensive tackle Broderick Washington is out due to an ankle injury that he sustained in Week 5. Despite a full week of practice as a full participant, rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane is also questionable. He may not be ready to play, as he is still being designated to return from IR. No other players have injury statuses for the game. Despite the laundry list of injuries reported, the Ravens will have most of their key players available. Two concerns arose on Thursday when wide receiver Zay Flowers appeared on the injury report with a toe ailment, and linebacker Mike Green joined him with a hamstring. Both were limited and were upgraded to full participants on Friday. Outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson is also making his return after undergoing a procedure to fix his broken finger. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter spoke about the defender, saying he is excited to get him back out on the field. (Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images) James Brizuela Fri, October 16, 2026 at 8:20 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Baltimore Ravens are gearing up for their divisional matchup with their former offensive coordinator-turned-head coach, Todd Monken, and his Cleveland Browns. The full final injury report is as follows: Jackson is still dealing with his sprained ankle and will now miss his second consecutive game. Joining Jackson is rookie tight end Matt Hibner, who suffered a hand injury. Reports indicate that Hibner has a cast on his hand, pointing to what could be a significant injury. There are no other red flags unless Jones or Vorhees are both unable to play, which would put the Baltimore offensive line in a very tough spot.

picks.headline: Why the Titans Will Beat the Colts in Week 6, Why They Won't, and a Prediction
picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Colts in Week 6, Why They Won't, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI For the fifth straight week in a row now, we can say that the Tennessee Titans fell short of expectations. What was initially painted as a bounce-back campaign for Robert Saleh and the franchise has turned into a recurring question from fans in Nashville: "How much longer will it take for this thing to change?" The answer? I wish I could give it to you. Instead, the Tennessee Titans stand alongside the Miami Dolphins as one of the only two teams without a win this season. On the road against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6, it no longer appears to be about things changing in the present. At this point, any sign of life on the way to a victory would do. In the split spirit of both optimism and reality, here's one reason the Titans will beat the Colts tomorrow, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction to split the difference. Will: Robert Saleh's defense bounces back Oct 11, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh walks onto the field during pre-game warmups against the Houston Texans at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Facing off with CJ Stroud and the Texans last Sunday, Robert Saleh's defense looked the worst they have all season. Saleh was in a direct battle with fellow defensive mind DeMeco Ryans, and beyond any doubt, he lost. Facing off with CJ Stroud and the Texans last Sunday, Robert Saleh's defense looked the worst they have all season. Saleh was in a direct battle with fellow defensive mind DeMeco Ryans, and beyond any doubt, he lost. Stroud threw for 261 yards and a score on 26 completions. The QB also found a touchdown on the ground as Houston ran away with a 26-3 victory. If Tennessee wins this week, it will be by slowing down a hot Colts offense with a massive recovery. Shut down Jonathan Taylor in the backfield, and who knows how far this team can get. Positively, Tennessee has done a solid job stopping the run this year in large part. The Texans rushed for just 79 yards last week in total. With star WR Alec Pierce on IR and reserve Ashton Dulin also set to miss time, QB Daniel Jones' options will be relatively limited. A Titans win would be about finding spurts of offensive momentum by way of defensive playmaking. Won't: Cam Ward continues to decline The lack of that offensive momentum, however, is the exact reason why Tennessee could come up short. Second-year QB Cam Ward has failed to generate any real momentum under center this season, and his shortcomings have the Titans punching up to begin with. Against Houston, Ward took four sacks and threw an interception for the third straight game. He's thrown less than 200 yards in four of the Titans' five games (five losses) this season. His full total is now out to three scores and three interceptions. That simply won't cut it for Tennessee's needed franchise QB. Promising weapons surrounding Ward, such as Wan'Dale Robinson and Carnell Tate in the WR room, haven't been able to elevate his underwhelming run. If the Titans fall short, you can safely bet it will be due to Ward once again falling short of the bar. Prediction: Titans lose, 27-17 Much like the Titans' early-season loss to the Texans last season (in which Tennessee went scoreless), I expect a relative surge of momentum from the offense. However, I don't expect the Titans to find a road win as they did vs. the Cardinals in 2025. Indy, while coming off a loss to the Steelers, has already collected two wins and consistently scored 20+ points. Their lone contest failing that margin came against Houston, in a 19-17 victory. Daniel Jones passes twice as much as Cam Ward (hardly hyperbole), and Taylor remains one of the NFL's premier backs. I predict Tennessee will surpass their three-point showing from Week 5, and things may even appear interesting early on. Still, there's nothing of present about this Titans team to suggest that a breakthrough is on the horizon. In an AFC South-bound duel tomorrow, I unfortunately anticipate the losing streak to continue. All we can hope for is a surprise from Saleh and a squad that, up to now, haven't done near enough to spark midseason hope. Gardner left the game during Tennessee’s opening possession of the second half after experiencing discomfort in his left leg. According to ESPN’s Stephen Holder, Gardner requested to leave the field before trainers began examining his left calf. The two-time All-Pro was subsequently taken to the locker room for further evaluation. The Colts held a 13-3 lead when Gardner exited during the third quarter. Gardner’s injury raises concerns for Colts defense Gardner eventually returned to the sideline and attempted to loosen up his injured leg, although his availability for the remainder of the contest remained uncertain. Cam Taylor-Britt replaced Gardner at outside cornerback, leaving Indianapolis without its top defensive back. The injury is particularly concerning because Gardner previously experienced calf problems during the 2025 season. Those issues forced him to miss several games after joining Indianapolis in a blockbuster trade with the New York Jets . The Colts surrendered two first-round draft selections and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell to acquire Gardner, demonstrating their commitment to strengthening the secondary. Gardner entered Sunday’s matchup having appeared in all six games this season. According to Colts Wire, opposing quarterbacks had completed nine of 17 passes targeting Gardner for 195 yards, while the veteran cornerback recorded three pass breakups. His ability to match up against opposing receivers makes him an important part of Indianapolis’ defensive strategy. Losing Gardner for an extended period could force the Colts to make significant adjustments in coverage, particularly against teams featuring explosive passing attacks. However, the immediate concern is determining the severity of his latest injury. With Indianapolis looking to remain competitive in the AFC South, keeping its defensive playmakers healthy will be critical. home.headline: Final injury report for Jets-Patriots: Will AJ Brown, Breece Hall play?
home.blurb: New York has ruled out Hall due to a quad injury as he will miss his third consecutive contest. With Hall sidelined once again, Allen will likely continue to have a larger role. The Jets have also ruled out wide receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger), edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) and offensive lineman Dylan Parham (knee). Sadiq has been listed as questionable due to a concussion and he is expected to play as long as he is able to clear concussion protocol ahead of Sunday’s game. Safety Dane Belton has also been listed as questionable due to a knee injury while wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. is questionable with an ankle injury. New England has listed Brown as questionable due to an ankle injury that he suffered in Week 1 and he is expected to return against the Jets. The Patriots have also listed Henderson as questionable due to an ankle injury that he suffered in Week 5 and if he is sidelined, Rhamondre Stevenson will likely have a larger role. Safety Craig Woodson (shoulder), linebacker Christian Elliss (chest), cornerback Channing Canada (hamstring) and tackles Will Campbell (knee) and Marcus Bryant (ankle) have all been listed as questionable. Cornerbacks Carlton Davis III (neck) and Karon Prunty (hamstring) have both been ruled out. Fans can catch Sunday afternoon’s matchup between the Jets and Patriots from Gillette Stadium at 1 p.m. ET on CBS in both teams’ home markets and select other locations across the country. Check local listings for games available in your area . The New England Patriots are at home Sunday afternoon as they host the New York Jets in a Week 6 AFC East matchup. New England enters Sunday’s contest with a 3-2 record after defeating the Las Vegas Raiders at home in dominant fashion in Week 5. Drake Maye led the way for the Patriots in their victory over the Raiders as he ended the game with 374 passing yards and five total touchdowns while Kyle Williams recorded 91 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown. The Patriots will try to grab another victory Sunday as they face off against the Jets in a tough home matchup. New York enters Sunday’s game with a 2-3 record after defeating the Cleveland Browns at home in Week 5. In their victory over the Browns, Geno Smith led the way for the Jets as he recorded 182 passing yards and one passing touchdown while Braelon Allen added 116 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown. While both teams are looking to pick up a victory in Sunday afternoon’s matchup, each may be without multiple key players due to injuries. Jets Injury Report: Will Breece Hall, Kenyon Sadiq Play? The Jets have seven players listed on their injury report, including running back Breece Hall and tight end Kenyon Sadiq. Patriots Injury Report: Will A.J. Brown, TreVeyon Henderson Play? The Patriots have nine players listed on their injury report, including wide receiver A.J. Brown and running back TreVeyon Henderson. The New England Patriots suffered a pair of concerning injury setbacks during Sunday's matchup against the New York Jets , with two former New York starters exiting against their old team. Right tackle Morgan Moses and left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker both sustained injuries during the Oct. 18 AFC East showdown at Gillette Stadium. Shortly afterward, Reiss reported another Patriots injury announcement , this time involving Vera-Tucker. The developments created an unusual storyline for New England, considering both players previously held starting roles with the Jets before making their way to the Patriots. The veteran previously started 16 games for the Jets in 2021 before returning for a second stint in 2024, when he made 14 starts at right tackle. He subsequently signed a three-year, $24 million contract with the Patriots and became a fixture along their offensive line. Moses started all 17 regular-season games and four playoff contests in 2025, providing much-needed stability for New England's offensive front. However, the veteran had been dealing with a foot injury entering Sunday's matchup. Vera-Tucker's injury had additional significance given his history in New York. The Saints have the league’s 20th-ranked offense (322.0 yards per game) and the 25th-ranked defense (361.0 yards per game) as they head into MetLife Stadium against a Giants team that has a chance to go 4-0 at home for the first time since 2008, when they got off to a 6-0 start at home. Despite the Saints’ struggles, they enter this game as a 1.5-point favorite per FanDuel , which is a head-scratcher considering they have averaged 21.3 points in their last three games, while the home team has averaged 25 points per game. But odds aside, the NFC East-leading Giants’ goal, according to head coach John Harbaugh, is simple: stack wins. “You always know what they are, but you know you’ve got to stack wins to make the December standings matter,” Harbaugh said when asked how much he pays attention to the standings at this point in the season. “So, we focus on the next game.” The Giants, according to Tankathon , have to make hay, so to speak. They face a remaining schedule with a combined winning percentage of .484, with their four toughest opponents being the 49ers, Jaguars, Lions, and Browns. All four of those challenging opponents land on the schedule after the Giants’ Week 8 bye. But to focus on what the Giants might do this week, let’s look at the best- and worst-case scenarios. If there was ever a good week for the Giants’ rushing game to snap out of its funk, this would be it. The league’s 30th-ranked run defense has struggled big time this season, allowing 4.9 yards per rushing attempt. It also ranks last in the league in defensive rush success (52.5%), meaning it struggles to stop opponents from gaining the minimum required yardage on a run (excluding kneeldowns and scrambles). The Giants’ rushing offense has not been the same since quarterback Jaxson Dart landed on IR with a season-ending knee injury. Although it ranks 17th in total rushing yards, it also averages a dismal 3.7 yards per attempt, 24th in the league. As if the rushing game’s struggles aren’t enough, it will be interesting to see if Harbaugh decides to reduce running back Cam Skattebo’s touches this week given his fumbling issue. As usual, the head coach was mum on the plans, but this could be a week when Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy Jr. get bigger roles in the rushing attack to see if they can jumpstart it. On the defensive side, the Giants’ pass rush has finally awakened after a slow start, recording seven sacks over the last two weeks. This week, they face a Saints offensive line that has surrendered three sacks to quarterback Tyler Shough over that same period. Combine that with the opportunistic Giants secondary, which has forced eight turnovers this season , against a Saints offense that has committed 13 giveaways, and the Giants’ quest to remain undefeated at home could get a lot easier. Why the Giants Won’t Beat the Saints Oct 5, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara (41) scores a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the first half at Caesars Superdome. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Giants’ run defense, in Harbaugh’s words, has been “feast or famine” this season. The Giants’ run defense, in Harbaugh’s words, has been “feast or famine” this season. Last week in the tie against Washington, it was clearly the latter, having surrendered a season-high 202 yards on the ground. There are many reasons for the Giants’ struggles in run defense, but one glaring issue has been facing pre-snap motion. Motion changes the look for the defense and has sometimes left players out of position or forced them into bad angles as they try to stop the play from gaining a lot of yards. Under head coach Kellen Moore, the Saints have deployed pre-snap motion on 64% of their offensive snaps this season, the ninth-highest rate in the league, and have a 46% success rate overall when using motion. While they use pre-snap motion more in the passing game, they have used it at a 35% rate in the rushing game. If the Giants, who have allowed opponents 5.2 yards per rush attempt on first down, can’t tighten that up, the Saints will have options on subsequent downs, giving New Orleans an advantage. The other thing that could spoil the Giants’ quest to win their fourth straight game at home is their own aggressiveness on defense. If the Giants, who over the last two weeks have blitzed on 57.8% of opposing quarterbacks’ drop backs, come at the Saints with a similar rate of pressure, they’d better hope that Saints signal-caller Tyler Shough, who per PFF data, has a 102.7 passer rating when throwing the ball in 2.5 seconds or less, doesn’t connect with receivers Chris Olave and Rashid Shaheed for the big pass plays downfield. If I live to be 100 (fingers crossed), I will never understand how the oddsmakers come up with their weekly point spreads. What I do understand is that Harbaugh has this team dialed in, and this matchup against the Saints is overall favorable for the Giants if they play a relatively clean game and keep the ball-security issues out of the mix. The Giants have a lot more going for them at this point in the season than the Saints, including far too many advantages that, if they hit on all cylinders, will get the job done. picks.blurb: Saints vs. Giants: Can New Orleans Snap Its Losing Streak? Our Staff Predicts Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The pressure continues to mount on the New Orleans Saints as they head to the Meadowlands for Sunday's Week 6 showdown against the New York Giants , desperately searching for answers amid a disappointing start to the season. Following a frustrating 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings , the Saints (1-4) have dropped three consecutive games, raising questions about the team's direction under second-year head coach Kellen Moore. The struggles have even drawn the attention of team owner Gayle Benson , who recently expressed frustration with the organization's performance and made it clear that continued losing would not be tolerated without consequences. With expectations rising and patience wearing thin, New Orleans faces another difficult challenge against a surprising Giants team that has emerged as an early contender in the NFC East. Here are our predictions for Sunday's game. Grant Chachere, Staff Writer: L 24-17 This is the Saints' first road game since Week 2, and it’s a strategic one at that, as the Saints will immediately fly out of New York for their game against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris next week. However, this is a critical game for coach Kellen Moore , and maybe even longtime general manager Mickey Loomis . I don’t think Tyler Shough will have many games like he did last week in the loss to the Vikings, but he will have another matchup against a top-10 defense as the Giants are ninth in total defense. The strength of the defense is its ability to defend the pass, allowing only 199.7 yards per contest, which is good for seventh in the NFL, and have forced six interceptions, which is good for fourth. While I think Shough will do much better, the Giants have the players needed to at least limit Shough, and New Orleans’ rushing attack is one of the NFL’s worst and will be ineffective. While the Giants have struggled to stop the run, they will have no trouble stopping the Saints. At the half, join us for Halftime Studs & Duds . Then, a fter the game, join us for our Biggest Winners & Biggest Losers , our View of the Game , and the Most Important Quotes from Kellen Moore & Players . Defensively, I think the Saints will do enough to keep the game close but not enough to win. The Giants aren’t the greatest offense in the world, but Cam Skattebo is a decent running back, while the receiving threats of Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are going to give the Saints’ defense a heap of trouble. I predict a one-score game in the Meadowlands with the Giants pulling it out. Prediction: Giants 24, Saints 17 Doug Joubert, Publisher: W 21-17 Which Saints club will show in the Meadowlands today? Will it be the one from the first three weeks of the season, or the one from the last three? We know this: those leading this organization have been put on notice by the woman that holds the checkbook. For the first time as owner of the Saints, Gayle Benson is faced with a situation that will require resolve and a possible move that will force her to make decisions that will be uncomfortable. She has put her trust and belief in those in charge. After seeing where her club has gone in the last few weeks, and the fan reaction to that direction, Mrs. Benson is having to rethink that trust. Meanwhile, a two-week road trip followed by the Saints open/bye week may be just what the doctor ordered for Moore and his troops: a chance to regroup and rethink where things are. Being a "glass-half-full" kinda guy, I'm getting this feeling this may be the first step to Moore, his coaches, and his players turning things around. However, don't bet the house on who I choose to win today. I've only been right once in five prognostications this year. Prediction: Saints 21 - Giants 17 Saints Mailbag Wednesdays, On SI Saints will answer your questions about what we see from our vantage point. To submit your thoughts or inquiries click here . The Saints are 1.5-point favorites over the Giants on the spread, with the over/under set at 45.5 total points. New Orleans has played a grueling schedule the last two weeks, facing the Falcons (who ran wild with Bijan Robinson) and the Vikings (who have one of the best defenses in the NFL). Jameis Winston has thrown for 694 yards with a 6:3 TD:INT ratio in the three games he's started. He's done a good job of feeding Malik Nabers as the Giants' WR1 has surpassed 100 receiving yards in each of the last two weeks. Of course, the thing with Winston is that he's prone to making critical mistakes when throwing into zone coverage. Without Jaxson Dart's mobility, the Giants simply haven't bee able to run the ball with Cam Skattebo, forcing Jameis Winston into high-variance, mistake-prone dropbacks. away.blurb: Hurts reportedly out for season As the New York Giants suffered a 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints in Week 6 on Sunday at MetLife Stadium, running back Cam Skattebo's time on the field was limited following an underwhelming display. Having lost his starting spot to Najee Harris, Skattebo featured in just six offensive snaps in the first half, spending a majority of the time on the bench. While the official starting lineups for the Giants' Week 7 game against the Texans are yet to be out, Skattebo's back-to-back lackluster performances make it highly unlikely that the running back will start again. “Got to Be Something Else Going On”: Analyst Speculates on Cam Skattebo’s Reduced Role After Giants’ Loss to Saints - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Cam Skattebo - Source: Instagram/@ sk4ttp4ck Farhaan Moulvi Mon, October 19, 2026 at 9:57 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads While his heavily reduced playtime could be linked to his below-par first-half performance, the running back revealed postgame that it was a consequence of his crucial overtime fumble in Week 5 against the Washington Commanders. However, sports commentator and former NFL MVP Boomer Esiason suggested that there could be other reasons behind Skattebo's reduced playing time. On the CBS Sports Network on Monday, the analyst speculated that the running back could have missed team meetings or failed to execute his assignments in the passing game. "Some of the issues that are surrounding Cam Skattebo are very interesting, you know. Yes, first and foremost they're trying to hold him accountable for the fumbling. There's no question about that. There's got to be something else going on. I don't know what else it is. It could be a couple late to meetings, it could be missed the assignments when it comes to the passing game," Esiason said (0:01). "There could be a lot of different things that the coaching staff is looking at and I would also think that they're making him understand you are going to be held accountable now," he further elaborated (0:33). Skattebo played just six offensive snaps, all in the first half of the game, and finished with no carries or targets to show for it. Will Cam Skattebo Start for the Giants in Week 7 vs Texans? While Skattebo's costly fumble against the Commanders got him a lot of flak from the NFL world, his next game against the Saints did not prove to be the redemption he would have hoped for. Cam Skattebo's performance against the New Orleans Saints was the first time in the running back's NFL career that he ended the game without a single touch. away.blurb: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Hurts reportedly out for season Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out? We're breaking down the final New Orleans Saints injury report for Week 6's road game against the New York Giants . Who's in, who's out, and who has a chance to play? The Giants ruled out safety Tyler Nubin (neck), tight end Theo Johnson (neck), and cornerback Colton Hood (concussion). WR Chris Olave (illness) didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but he was able to work on a limited basis during Friday's practice. He should play so long as that illness is behind him. DL Nathan Shepherd (illness) also missed two days of practice with an illness that's been going around the locker room. He was limited on Friday as well. CB Lorenzo Styles Jr. (knee) was limited on both Thursday and Friday, so don't be surprised if he's a game-time decision. RB Alvin Kamara (back) practiced on limited reps throughout the week. The Saints didn't bring up either of the two running b acks on their practice squad so it does llook like he'll play. Starting offensive linemen Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) are both questionable for the Giants, as is edge rusher Abdul Carter (calf). There's a crowd of Giants players available to play after being listed on the injury report this week: cornerback Greg Newsome II (groin), outside linebacker Malik Harrison (groin), defensive back Elijah Campbell (thumb), running back Najee Harris (ribs), tight end Isaiah Likely (foot), wide receivers Darnell Mooney (neck) and Charlie Jones (Achilles), as well as safety Jason Pinnock (concussion). As was the case last week, the following Saints players are on injured reserve with season-ending injuries: defensive tackle Bryan Bresee, running back Ty Chandler, cornerback David Long Jr., tight end Moliki Matavao, offensive lineman Dillon Radunz, and cornerback Rejzohn Wright. However, a couple of others have been designated to return after sitting out at least four games: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and veteran running back Travis Etienne Jr. are both expected to return after the bye week in November but it sounds like we won't see left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. until December at the soonest. Offensive lineman Nick Saldiveri is on the season-ending PUP list (physically unable to perform), while wide receiver Mason Tipton is eligible to return after missing four games. Tipton has not returned to practice yet. This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: Breaking down the Saints-Giants injury report: Who's in, who's out? home.headline: New York Giants' Latest Injury Concern is Beyond Terrifying
home.blurb: Hurts reportedly out for season The New York Giants have dealt with enough injury issues this year. Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns are both out for the season. Andrew Thomas is nursing a groin issue. Jermaine Eluemunor just hurt his calf. The secondary is banged up. Abdul Carter did not practice on Wednesday due to a calf injury, and while head coach John Harbaugh said Carter is "doing very well," it's hard not to be worried. Harbaugh doesn't sound too concerned, so hopefully, it's just something minor and Carter is being held out as a precautionary measure. New York Giants' Latest Injury Concern is Beyond Terrifying - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL New York Giants' Latest Injury Concern is Beyond Terrifying (Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images) Matthew Schmidt Thu, October 15, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads But just when you thought it couldn't get any worse for the Giants, another alarming injury concern popped up on Wednesday. Calf issues can be tricky, and for a player like Carter who relies heavily on his explosiveness and burst, it can become a very serious problem. But the Giants are already without Burns, and Kayvon Thibodeaux has been a non-factor through the first five games. The last thing New York's ailing pass rush needs is for Carter to be sidelined, too. Carter has logged two sacks and six quarterback hits thus far, so it's not like he's been a game-wrecker. But he has been, by far, the Giants' best pass rusher, and he was No. 3 overall pick in 2025 for a reason. New York has managed just eight sacks as a team heading into Week 6, which ranks toward the bottom of the NFL. Obviously, losing Burns — who racked up 16.5 sacks a year ago — is devastating. But the Giants should still be generating more pressure with Carter and Thibodeaux than they have. It would certainly help if Thibodeaux were more effective . The 25-year-old has posted six tackles and no sacks, and his lone quarterback hit came back in Week 1. You would never know this is the same Thibodeaux that rattled off 11.5 sacks in 2023 and appeared to be an up-and-coming star at the time. For now, though, the Giants absolutely Carter on the field, not just because Thibodeaux has been struggling, but because Carter is supposed to be New York's next star defender. Carter was one of five Giants players to miss practice Wednesday, with Thomas, Eluemunor, Colton Hood and Tyler Nubin being the others. New York will be hosting the 1-4 New Orleans Saints this Sunday and will have a brilliant opportunity to improve to 4-1-1 and bolster its standing at the top of the NFC East. Hopefully, Carter is able to take the gridiron for Big Blue.

home.headline: “Got to Be Something Else Going On”: Analyst Speculates on Cam Skattebo’s Reduced Role After Giants’ Loss to Saints
home.blurb: Hurts reportedly out for season As the New York Giants suffered a 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints in Week 6 on Sunday at MetLife Stadium, running back Cam Skattebo's time on the field was limited following an underwhelming display. Having lost his starting spot to Najee Harris, Skattebo featured in just six offensive snaps in the first half, spending a majority of the time on the bench. While the official starting lineups for the Giants' Week 7 game against the Texans are yet to be out, Skattebo's back-to-back lackluster performances make it highly unlikely that the running back will start again. “Got to Be Something Else Going On”: Analyst Speculates on Cam Skattebo’s Reduced Role After Giants’ Loss to Saints - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Cam Skattebo - Source: Instagram/@ sk4ttp4ck Farhaan Moulvi Mon, October 19, 2026 at 9:57 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads While his heavily reduced playtime could be linked to his below-par first-half performance, the running back revealed postgame that it was a consequence of his crucial overtime fumble in Week 5 against the Washington Commanders. However, sports commentator and former NFL MVP Boomer Esiason suggested that there could be other reasons behind Skattebo's reduced playing time. On the CBS Sports Network on Monday, the analyst speculated that the running back could have missed team meetings or failed to execute his assignments in the passing game. "Some of the issues that are surrounding Cam Skattebo are very interesting, you know. Yes, first and foremost they're trying to hold him accountable for the fumbling. There's no question about that. There's got to be something else going on. I don't know what else it is. It could be a couple late to meetings, it could be missed the assignments when it comes to the passing game," Esiason said (0:01). "There could be a lot of different things that the coaching staff is looking at and I would also think that they're making him understand you are going to be held accountable now," he further elaborated (0:33). Skattebo played just six offensive snaps, all in the first half of the game, and finished with no carries or targets to show for it. Will Cam Skattebo Start for the Giants in Week 7 vs Texans? While Skattebo's costly fumble against the Commanders got him a lot of flak from the NFL world, his next game against the Saints did not prove to be the redemption he would have hoped for. Cam Skattebo's performance against the New Orleans Saints was the first time in the running back's NFL career that he ended the game without a single touch.
