away.headline: Dee Winters Injury Update is Bad News for Dallas Cowboys Defense
away.blurb: Winters is coming off a game against Green Bay where he had his first interception of the season, one that he appeared to return for a touchdown before replay went back and ruled him down. But on top of that, the Cowboys are still without linebacker DeMarvion Overshown due to a hamstring injury. Fortunately, there's a chance he makes his return from a five-game absence in Week 7 against the Philadelphia Eagles, but hamstrings can be tough to fully bounce back from, especially for a player with an injury history like Overshown's. Who Steps Up at LB for Dallas Cowboys With Dee Winters Out? With Winters out, fans should expect rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham take on an even bigger role than he already had, but this will also impact the depth behind him. DeMarvion Overshown Injury Update: Cowboys Star LB Could Return in Week 6 The Dallas Cowboys are coming off another embarrassing loss, as they fell to the Green Bay Packers in a 23-13 finish at Lambeau Field on Sunday night. But to make matters worse, the Cowboys lost starting linebacker Dee Winters to an injury during the game. Winters has an Achiles strain, an injury that will force him to "likely miss" Week 7's matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football, per Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer. Dee Winters Injury Timing is Bad For Dallas The injury timing is unfortunate for multiple reasons. The Cowboys defense is already dreadful as is, so they can't afford to have a starter like Winters miss extended time. Hopefully the team gets him back sooner rather than later. So far this season, Winters has started all six games while posting 35 total tackles (23 solo), one fumble recovery and one interception. Schottenheimer praised Shemar James and Justin Barron while speaking with the media on Monday. Both players could take on larger roles with Winters set to miss time. "We're getting a lot of guys reps. Shemar James, like I said, is doing a really good job," Schottenheimer said. "Justin Barron last night did a really good job. We put him in on a couple passing situations. They actually tried him on a little wheel route immediately when he came in the game and he played it beautifully. That's a position that normally gets dinged up and beat up a little bit, and both those guys Shemar and Justin have played really well for us." The Cowboys and Eagles will kick off from Lincoln Financial Field on Monday Night Football in Week 7 at 7:15 p.m. CT/ Dallas Cowboys Injury Updates After Week 6 Loss Include Another Starting Defender Brian Schottenheimer Deflects Taking Accountability For Latest Cowboys Failure Dallas Cowboys' Highest & Lowest Graded Players in Week 6 Loss vs Packers Von Miller Takes Accountability For Disappointing Start With Dallas Cowboys This article was originally published on www.si.com/nfl/cowboys/onsi as Dee Winters Injury Update is Bad News for Dallas Cowboys Defense .

away.headline: Dallas Cowboys Injury Updates After Week 6 Loss Include Another Starting Defender
away.blurb: Dee Winters suffered what was labeled an ankle injury in the first half of the Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers and the veteran wasn't able to return after that. It figures that Winters would get hurt during a game in which he made an impact play with an interception he nearly returned for a touchdown. Winters wasn't the only notable player to get hurt, as wideout and returner KaVontae Turpin came down with a ribs injury on the opening kickoff and did not return, either. The Cowboys replaced Turpin with wide receiver Jonathan Mingo on punt returns and running back Tyler Goodson on kickoffs. The former averaged six yards per return and had a long of 16 yards and the latter broke off a 30-yard return and averaged 24.4 pre return over five attempts. Putting that aside for now, Overshown finally returned to practice last week and turned in two limited sessions in total, so it appears he's at least getting closer to returning. That said, we have expected Overshown back for a few weeks now, yet the veteran is still out, so nobody should get their hopes up for Overshown returning to the field this week. I’ve figured out how to use it on the field, figured out the right techniques, figured out the right stance to get into and just started striking blocks and making sure they went backwards.” New Packers Defensive Tackle Will Have Micah Parsons’ Seal of Approval Skip to main content SI.COM GREEN BAY, Wis. – There might be nobody happier about the Green Bay Packers’ decision to sign Mazi Smith to the practice squad on Monday than his former-turned-current teammate, Micah Parsons. As reported by ESPN.com’s Rob Demovsky , the Packers signed Smith to the practice squad following a Monday workout. “Let’s go!” Parsons screamed when the Cowboys drafted Smith in the first round in 2023. Parsons with the Packers has been the hype man for Lukas Van Ness, among others. He was the same way with Smith during their time together. “NO MORE QB SNEAKS AJ!” @MicahhParsons11 told Cowboys DC Dan Quinn to pick Michigan's Mazi Smith earlier today and IT HAPPENED 😂 pic.twitter.com/nGm62CAnDK Smith was a bust for the Cowboys and represents a Hail Mary of sorts for the Packers on a talented player who could fill a need. The Packers have been hammered by injuries at defensive tackle, with Warren Brinson, Javon Hargrave and Jonathan Ford on injured reserve. They beat the Cowboys with only four defensive tackles on the active roster. Plus, they have only one player on the practice squad, undrafted rookie David Blay Jr. So, maybe the Packers will catch lightning in a model with Smith, who was the 26th pick of the 2023 draft. "It's like Christmas," then-Cowboys coach Mike McCarthy said after Smith was selected. “When you look at all the work that goes into it, going back to his 30 visit, and just what a great fit he is for us … I just want him to be himself. He is a great fit for us.” Micah Parsons Was In His Corner During the predraft process, Smith gained a big supporter in Parsons. He even texted his defensive coordinator at the time, Dan Quinn, hoping the Cowboys would draft Smith. “It’s not what I think he can be, it’s what Mazi has to be,” Parsons said at the start of training camp in 2024 . “When you get to this business, there is no more of a choice or a can, it’s either you will or you won’t. home.headline: Packers rumors: Adam Schefter suggests Micah Parsons still weeks away from return
home.blurb: Schefter went on to state that Parsons likely wouldn’t be back until at least early next month. His knee injury has kept him on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list the entire season. While it would have been quite the storyline if Parsons returned this past Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys, his former team, his 21-day practice window still has not opened up. Before the ex-Cowboy can make his return, that window must open up. With a pivotal Sunday afternoon tilt against the Lions approaching, it sounds as if Parsons will continue his stint on the PUP. If Schefter’s timeline is correct, the earliest the Packers would get Parsons back could be in New England against the Patriots on November 8th. Green Bay’s bye is two weeks after that. It feels more likely that the former first-rounder will return against the Los Angeles Rams in a primetime matchup on Thanksgiving Eve. In any case, the sooner the Pack gets Parsons back, the better. Their postseason hopes may depend on it. At 4-2, the Green Bay Packers are tied with the Chicago Bears for second place in the NFC North. The duo are a game and a half behind the Minnesota Vikings at 5-0. Riding a three-game winning streak, the Packers will travel to Detroit to take on the Lions in a divisional clash. The Lions are right behind Green Bay at 3-2. They’ll also be fresh, coming off a bye week. While the Pack prepares for a pivotal matchup, they received an update on star edge rusher Micah Parsons . Per ESPN’s Adam Schefter on the Pat McAfee Show, Parsons is still at least a couple of weeks away from returning. McAfee shared Schefter’s report via X, formerly Twitter. “I was told that Micah Parsons wasn’t close to playing against the Dallas Cowboys,” Schefter said on the show. “They haven’t opened up his practice window yet, and I’m not anticipating that right now.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Like ClutchPoints’ content? home.blurb: Green Bay is signing defensive tackle Mazi Smith to the practice squad after injuries thinned out what was once a crowded room on the interior. The Green Bay Packers are signing former first-round defensive tackle Mazi Smith to the practice squad. ESPN reporter Rob Demovsky first reported the signing. The move addresses a depth issue that developed on the interior of the defensive line over the first weeks of the season. Smith was the 26th pick of the 2023 NFL Draft , selected by the Dallas Cowboys out of Michigan. Dallas traded Smith to the New York Jets in 2025. Earlier this year, he spent time with the Miami Dolphins, mostly on the practice squad, and he appeared in one game for them. Miami released him last week. Once he became available, the Packers decided to bring him in, because the defensive tackle depth has become a real concern. The Packers searching for help at this spot isn't much of a surprise. They started the season with seven defensive tackles on the 53-man roster, a number that looked like a comfortable cushion at the time. Since then, the injuries piled up. Warren Brinson and Jonathan Ford both went on injured reserve. They are expected to potentially return down the stretch of the season. Javon Hargrave, meanwhile, is out for the season with an Achilles rupture. Jordon Riley started the season on the PUP list after rupturing his Achilles late last season. He’s been designed for return and is expected to come back at some point fairly soon. At this exact moment, though, Green Bay has only four defensive tackles on the 53-man roster: Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks, Chris McClellan, and Anthony Campbell. David Blay Jr. is also on the practice squad. The Packers have been looking for options, and Smith can be that extra body with a high pedigree . Packers turn to a former first-round pick to patch a sudden depth problem, but his NFL track record raises fair questions Skip to content College Football Close Menu All College Football A pedigree that hasn't translated Smith entered the league as a high-end prospect, but he hasn't been successful in the NFL so far. In his two full seasons with the Cowboys, he generated eight pressures in both 2023 and 2024. That's fairly decent pass rush production for a rotational interior player. The big problem was run defense. Smith posted poor performances against the run in Dallas, and that deficiency has followed him throughout his career. His time with the Dolphins didn't offer much new information either. He played only nine defensive snaps in one game, the Week 4 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings. He didn't generate any pressures and had little impact in that game. For the most part, Smith lines up in the B-gap, but he can also align as a nose tackle in the A-gap. He took on a lot of nose tackle snaps for the Cowboys in 2024, his second season. Despite the early struggles, the Packers believe the 6-foot-3, 337-pound defensive tackle can still develop. home.headline: Packers vs. Cowboys: Breaking down final injury report of Week 6
home.blurb: LG Aaron Banks (toe/knee): He practiced in a limited capacity all week, but it's his first week back from a multi-week injury. More than likely, the Packers will go with Laken Tomlinson at left guard against the Cowboys. Eventually, the Packers will have to make a long-term decision on their preferred starter at the position. DL Anthony Campbell (ankle) : His likely return from an ankle injury is coming at a good time considering the injury situation along the defensive front. It's possible Campbell will need to play double-digit snaps behind Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks and Chris McClellan on Sunday night. CB Brandon Cisse (hip): An unexpected addition to the injury report. Cisse injured his hip and was limited on Friday, creating the dreaded late-week injury and potential need to scramble for answers at a key position. Carrington Valentine would likely start if Cisse can't go. Depth at cornerback is under real stress ahead of matchup with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. WR Savion Williams (ankle): Is the second-year receiver ready to return from an ankle injury that had him on injured reserve to start the season? A natural replacement option for Skyy Moore, who is out, Williams could provide help as a gadget weapon on offense and in the return game if the Packers activate him to the 53-man roster before Sunday night. WR/KR Skyy Moore (ankle): The Packers' primary kick and punt returner injured his ankle last week and wasn't able to practice this week. It's possible the Packers will activate Savion Williams to help make up for Moore's absence in the return game and at receiver. The Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant and rookie offensive lineman Drew Shelton and listed linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, defensive lineman L.T Overton, cornerback Joey Porter Jr. and cornerback Ameer Speed as questionable on the final injury report. Receiver CeeDee Lamb (thigh) does not have an status designation and will play. How will the injury situation affect Sunday night's showdown with the Cowboys? Here’s an in-depth breakdown of the Packers ’ final injury report ahead of Week 6: OL Jacob Monk (quad): He's no longer a starting option at right guard, where Travis Glover or Kevin Zeitler will start Sunday, but Monk could be a backup at center and get snaps on special teams protection units if he's healthy. DL Jordon Riley (Achilles): He only just returned to practice this week, and even though the Packers need help along the defensive line, Riley is unlikely to play Sunday. He could be a factor as a run stuffer come next week or Week 8. DL Jonathan Ford (calf): His injury, combined with the season-ending injury to Javon Hargrave, puts the Packers in a tough place along the defensive front. Ford likely would have played a lot of snaps on Sunday if healthy. DL Javon Hargrave (Achilles): The veteran suffered a season-ending Achilles tendon injury last Sunday and will eventually go on injured reserve, possibly as soon as Saturday. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights San Francisco can improve to 6-0 and strengthen its NFC West lead, while Washington enters Levi's Stadium looking to pull off a sizable road upset Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Monday Night Football," the San Francisco 49ers play host to the Washington Commanders . San Francisco is riding high atop the NFC West with a 5-0 record, having defeated the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in a barnburner last week. The Niners have battled injuries on both sides of the ball all season, yet have remained unbeaten. They can create a three-game lead in the division with a victory on Monday night. Washington is coming off an absolute debacle last Sunday against the New York Giants , wherein the Commanders had a chance to kick a field goal to win the game at the end of overtime, but bungled the clock management as badly as any team you'll ever see. The Commies are just 1-3-1 entering this game, and they're looking to avoid falling further into the basement in the NFC East. Will the Niners continue to roll, or will the Commanders pull off the upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch 49ers vs. Commanders live Date: Monday, Oct. 19 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: Levi's Stadium (Santa Clara, California) TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: 49ers -7.5, O/U 52.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Commanders have the ball Jayden Daniels looked no worse for wear last week in his return from another dislocated elbow. He completed 17 of 25 passes for 199 yards, while also rushing nine times for 103 yards and two touchdowns. Had he and the entire offense not totally brain-farted at the end of overtime, it would have been a wildly encouraging performance for Washington's rest-of-season outlook. While Daniels has been excellent when taking off to run in his three starts, Washington's running backs have been extremely inefficient on the ground. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (who was ruled out for this game after not practicing all week), Rachaad White , Austin Ekeler and the recently-released Kaytron Allen have combined to average just 3.7 yards per carry. The offensive line has created little push up front, with the backs collectively gaining just 0.95 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, and the backs themselves have broken tackles at the second-lowest rate in all of football. The 49ers, meanwhile, have allowed just 3.7 yards per rush to enemy running backs, with great tackling being the primary method of limiting yardage. Backs have gained 1.47 yards per carry before contact (an above-average mark), but only 2.22 yards after contact thanks to the lowest broken-tackle rate in the league. As a result, San Francisco has allowed only two explosive runs all season, per Tru Media, the fewest in the NFL . San Francisco has also been mostly strong against the pass, checking in 10th in opponents' EPA per dropback and 5th in opponents' success rate. The 49ers have allowed quarterbacks to complete only 64.4% of their passes at an average of 6.1 yards per attempt, with just five touchdowns and three interceptions in five games. It's tough to know what to make of Washington's passing game because it hasn't been at full strength for most of the season. Daniels missed two-and-a-half games. Chig Okonwko missed two. Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs each missed one and saw their snaps limited in another. The Daniels-McLaurin-Diggs trio has shared the field for only 57 plays so far this season, according to Tru Media. Daniels is just 15 of 30 for 129 yards on those plays, but he has thrown for three scores and scrambled for 62 yards. Daniels should, in theory, see at least some clean pockets with the 49ers again playing without Nick Bosa , but Washington's offensive line has yielded pressure on over 38% of dropbacks so far this season, so the Niners could have a chance to get into Daniels' lap and force him into tough throws and mistakes. With the generally sticky coverage the San Francisco corners have played so far this season, it could be tough sledding for Washington in the passing game on Monday night. When the 49ers have the ball San Francisco has been the league's fourth-most efficient offense by EPA per play, according to Tru Media, ranking second with the pass and 14th with the run. Brock Purdy is playing at as high a level as any quarterback in football, completing 69% of his passes at an average of 8.4 yards per attempt with a league-high 13 touchdown passes and just two interceptions. Purdy also has a 57.9% passing success rate, which ranks as the best in the league. Purdy has done that despite hemorrhaging wide receivers throughout the season. Ricky Pearsall was lost for the year in training camp. Christian Kirk (listed as questionable for this week) has yet to make his 49er debut. De'Zhaun Stribling was injured in Week 1. Demarcus Robinson went down in Week 2. Deebo Samuel and Jacob Cowing were knocked out of last week's win over the Seahawks. Mike Evans has been playing through a painful rib injury. (He's also questionable for Monday night.) George Kittle spent the first two weeks ramping up to a full workload after last season's Achilles tear. And yet, here the 49ers are. Washington, meanwhile, has been one of the league's friendliest pass defenses. Every team the Commanders have faced has thrown for at least 257 net yards. Four of the five teams have gone more than 300 and two of them exceeded 400. The Commanders have allowed opponents to complete 65.2% of passes at an average of 7.1 yards per attempt, with 14 touchdowns and just three interceptions. The 103.9 passer rating against the Commanders to date is the sixth-worst mark in the league. It's very easy to see San Francisco finding success through the air so long as Evans suits up for the game. Christian McCaffrey is sharing the workload in the run game far more this season than in years past, with 61 carries for 286 yards againt Kaelon Black's 37 carries for 136 yards. McCaffrey's 4.7 yards-per-carry average is far better than what he posted over the last two years (4.0 and 3.9), and his rushing success rate of 45.9% is seventh-best out of 48 qualifying running backs. That figure is the second-best mark of his career, behind only the 2023 season, during which he led the NFL in rushing yards. The Commanders have actually been stingy against the run this year, allowing only 3.9 yards per carry, with opposing backs limited to 0.69 yards per attempt before contact by the defensive front. Washington having similar success stopping the run here is important because it could make the 49ers one-dimensional, but the Commanders' pass-funnel defense also plays right into San Francisco's hands because of how efficient the 49ers' passing game has been so far this year. Purdy and Co. should eat, even if McCaffrey doesn't. I picked against the 49ers last week and regretted it almost immediately after seeing how their offense struggled against the stingy Seattle defense. Needless to say, Washington's defense is not of the same quality. I know the 49ers are still hemorrhaging wide receivers, but as long as Brock Purdy, Mike Evans, George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey are healthy and Kyle Shanahan is calling the plays, they are going to move the ball efficiently. And I don't trust the Commanders to do quite enough to keep up with their explosive offense.
